summary: This is a Makefile snippet that sets up shell configuration and defines a bash target. It declares that the default action is to show help, establishes a color constant for yellow text, and creates a bash target that prints an informational message about starting an interactive shell in Docker.

explanations.1: SHELL:=bash tells Make to use bash as the shell interpreter instead of the default sh when executing commands.
explanations.4: default: help means when someone runs 'make' without arguments, it will run the 'help' target instead of the first target in the file.
explanations.6: COLOR_YELLOW:=33 is a variable storing the ANSI color code for yellow, which will be used later to colorize terminal output.
explanations.8: .PHONY: bash tells Make that 'bash' is not a real file to be created, just a label for a command to run.
explanations.10: @printf uses ANSI escape codes (the \e[...m parts) to print colored text; the @ symbol prevents Make from echoing the command itself before running it.
